items.title: Bob Havens interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997
items.q: Ten years before this John and I were students in a music camp, Interlochen Music Camp in Michigan.

ctx.x: Okay. Well I’ll just briefly say that trombone became my favorite instrument. I played the violin all the way through high school and even a little with the local symphony afterwards. But trombone became my favorite and I eventually dropped the violin all together. And my father brought home a record from his place where he worked, and it was a Red Nichols and the Five Pennies recording. And on that record was Jack Teagarden. That was my first introduction to the sound of Jack Teagarden. And this was about 1947 I…

Guard from Illinois, and I was in the Division band, the marching band. Then when I got out of the Army I went to work as a radio repairman in a local shop and playing music at night. Finally in 1955 I got a phone call and it was a man by the name of John Strophe. Ten years before this John and I were students in a music camp, Interlochen Music Camp in Michigan. Well we never corresponded after that. And here ten years had elapsed and he was playing with the Ralph Flanagan Orchestra, traveling through Quincy…
